featured_reviews.name: sagar jadhav
featured_reviews.review_text:
This was my third visit to Santosham, and it continues to be a great spot for comforting, authentic South Indian food!
If you are looking for a complete traditional experience, their unlimited South Indian Thali is a must-try at least once. It’s a beautifully simple, home-style meal that tastes amazing. The thali comes fully loaded with a variety of authentic items—hot puris, steamed rice, flavorful and piping hot Sambar, a wonderfully tangy Rasam, and traditional sabjis like a dry Beans and Carrot Poriyal and a comforting Cabbage Kootu. They round it out with crisp appalams, fresh curd, pickle, and a sweet Payasam to finish it off. Just a quick heads-up: they have different pricing for the unlimited thali on weekdays versus weekends.
While the thali is fantastic and incredibly generous, it is quite a heavy meal. Personally, since we lean more toward classic South Indian snacks rather than massive authentic meals, the thali is a 'try it once for the experience' item for us.
If you aren't super hungry or just prefer lighter fare, absolutely go for their Idli and Dosa options instead. They are perfectly prepared and hit the spot every time. I also have to give a massive shoutout to their Dal Wada—it is incredibly crispy on the outside, perfectly spiced, and just flat-out delicious.

Staff is very helpful, one of the staff saw I m not adding Green chutney on rice, he came and suggested to use green chutney over the rice and it really tasted so good 😊
Overall verdict: Come hungry for the grand unlimited thali at least once, but you'll find yourself coming back regularly for the stellar dosas, idlis, and that amazing dal wada!

featured_reviews.name: Manikandan
featured_reviews.review_text: Santosham - Satvik South Indian Restaurant near Marine Drive is a clean and comforting spot for authentic South Indian vegetarian food in South Mumbai. The restaurant keeps a simple, traditional feel without trying to be overly fancy, and the food is the main highlight. Located in Marine Lines, it’s convenient after a walk along Marine Drive or nearby sightseeing. featured_reviews.name: RACHNA TULI MASHKARIA
featured_reviews.review_text:
The banana leaf thali is not just a meal – it’s an experience that blends flavor, tradition, and hospitality in the most wholesome way. Served on a fresh banana leaf, the thali immediately brings a sense of authenticity and connection to Indian culinary roots.

What makes it truly special is the variety. From fragrant rice and comforting dals to vibrant curries, tangy pickles, crispy papad, and a sweet finish, every dish complements the other beautifully. The balance of flavors – spicy, tangy, salty, and sweet – ensures that every bite feels satisfying. The banana leaf itself adds a subtle earthy aroma while also being eco-friendly and hygienic.

Another highlight is the cultural warmth associated with it. The way servers lovingly add refills, encouraging you to eat to your heart’s content, makes the experience feel both generous and personal.

Overall, the banana leaf thali is not just good – it’s nourishing, soulful, and a celebration of food as tradition. Whether you’re a food enthusiast or someone who loves comfort meals, it’s definitely worth trying.

featured_reviews.name: Sarah Chamdawala
featured_reviews.review_text:
We had an amazing authentic South Indian breakfast at Santosham! Ordered the Mysore sada dosa, which was crispy and spicy and delicious; the ghee podi idli was fluffy and you could really taste the shuddh ghee; the beetroot rawa dosa was soo crispy and had just the perfect little hint of beetroot flavour; the benne dosa was yum and perfectly crispy on the outside and fluffy on the inside and served with the most decadent pure white butter! The filter coffees (both cold and hot) were also delicious with the perfect froth on top! We also enjoyed the rose milk with chia seeds. The tomato chutney, coconut chutney and sambhar served on the side were also great and proved the perfect accompaniments to the meal.
A special mention for the service which was top notch, thanks to Nasim and Uday who were very helpful and quick.
10/10 would recommend this place!

The Rameshwaram Cafe is a beloved South Indian vegetarian restaurant brand known for serving authentic, traditional flavours in a modern, vibrant setting. With a focus on quality ingredients, quick service, and consistency, The Rameshwaram Cafe has become a go-to destination for comfort food lovers blending nostalgia, devotion, and deliciousness in every bite.

featured_reviews.name: Suraj Jobanputra
featured_reviews.review_text:
Everything was just perfect!

Every single dish we ordered was simply amazing. Here is a breakdown of the highlights:
The Iconic Dosas & Idlis: The Ghee Podi Idli was cloud-soft, drenched in flavorful ghee, and packed a perfect spicy punch with the podi. The Benne Butter Masala Dosa was perfectly crisp on the outside, fluffy on the inside, and rich in flavor.
The Chutneys: A special shoutout to their signature chutneys—fresh, vibrant, and the perfect accompaniment to the main dishes.
The Grand Finale: You cannot leave this place without trying their Coffee Ice Cream. It is an absolute game-changer! It perfectly captures the rich, bold, and aromatic essence of traditional filter coffee but in a creamy, refreshing frozen dessert. It’s not overly sweet, making it the ultimate treat for true coffee lovers.
The service was incredibly fast despite the bustling crowd, and the quality of ingredients truly shines through in every bite.

Verdict: Exceptional food, vibrant vibes, and a 10/10 experience. Whether you are going for a heavy breakfast or a sweet evening treat, this place never disappoints. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Jubin B
featured_reviews.review_text:
Rameshwaram Cafe has been on my list for a while, though I walked in with some hesitation given the mixed reviews online. Glad to say, the experience leaned positive.

We ordered the Benne Pudi Masala Dosa, Benne Masala Dosa, Ghee Pudi Idli, and the Filter Coffee Softy. The dosas arrived crisp, generously buttered, and well-balanced in flavour, while the Ghee Pudi Idli stood out for its richness and depth. The Filter Coffee Softy was an interesting, indulgent twist—worth trying for something different.

What works here is consistency in taste and a certain indulgent South Indian profile that’s clearly designed to appeal to a wider palate. However, the pricing does sit on the higher side for this category, which slightly affects the overall value equation.

I visited on a Monday around 3 PM and was seated in about 30 minutes—manageable by their standards. That said, this isn’t a place I’d personally queue up for on a busy weekend. It’s best experienced when the rush is relatively controlled.

If you’re in that part of the city, it’s definitely worth a visit once—more for the experience than as a regular go-to.

featured_reviews.name: anwesa banerjee
featured_reviews.review_text: This review has been long overdue!! I visited the Rameshwaram cafe in Mumbai twice since it opened, and if has been extremely memorable each time.. not just because because of the food, that is soul-soothing as ever!! But what really stood out each time was the hospitality of the staff!! You can see the crowd that gathers outside each day eager to taste the sumptuous food inside and that too in the Mumbai heat and humidity.. that itself is a testament to the quality of food I suppose. But it is the staff who go above and beyond to make the experience as rewarding.. right from the people managing the crowd at the entrance, offering a seat to an aged couple as they wait in line or simply accommodating our request in the sweetest way to allow us seats in a fully booked restaurant just so that our friend (leaving for the UK the very next day) doesn't have to miss out on the experience. Even the founders happened to stop by on our first visit for feedback.. and three happy, tummy-full-soul-satisfied customers expressed sincere gratitude to them. The wait maybe really long on certain days.. but it is just worth the hassle!!

featured_reviews.name: Tarun Joseph
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Rameshwaram Cafe at Churchgate this morning for a quick breakfast like old times.
I’m a Kannadiga and I've lived in Bengaluru for a couple of years and used to visit Rameshwaram Cafe (Indiranagar and JP Nagar outlets), at least once a month. Even now, whenever I go back to Bengaluru, it’s a mandatory stop. So when they announced they were opening in Mumbai, I was genuinely excited. I’ve been missing proper dosa and idli here.

But what I ate today was not Rameshwaram Cafe.

I ordered my usual ghee pudi plain dosa and there was barely any pudi on it. The taste was completely off. It didn’t have the flavour, the texture, or even the smell that makes Rameshwaram Cafe what it is. The taste just felt different, very different. It honestly didn’t even feel like the Rameshwaram Cafe I remember from Bengaluru.
I didn’t try the pudi idli myself, but my friends ordered it and said it was just average as well.

After all the hype, the long queues, and the name they’ve built in Bengaluru, this was unbelievably disappointing. If this is what Rameshwaram Cafe Mumbai is serving, they’re just riding on the Bengaluru brand while delivering something far below that standard.

A truly mediocre experience. If you’ve actually eaten at the Bengaluru outlet, this will feel like a huge downgrade.

featured_reviews.name: Bhavin Parekh
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Society is one of the finest restaurant in the Iconic and legendary hotel - The Ambassador since 1949 at a 5min walking distance from Churchgate station near Marine Drive. The Society restaurant gives a royal outlook with its grandeur decor, elegant luminous chandeliers and cosy seatings makes this place ideal for a peaceful dining with family and loved ones.
This place is serving delectable delicacies of North Indian and Continental cuisines since 1949 and now Oriental and Asian cuisines adds to their classic menu giving more flavours and culinary aromas to the food lovers. The menu is curated well by their sous chef and executive chef keeping the likings and taste of their guests.
I was fortunate to experience their few asian food dishes of the new oriental menu. All food preparation was finest and perfect with fantastic taste making the dining blissful and memorable.
Oriental food 🍜tried 👇🏻

Soup and Salad
▪️Lemon Coriander soup - A perfect thing to start the meal ... A soup made with veggies like bell pepper, babycorn, carrot, spring onions and zucchini was scrumptious
▪️Tom Yam Phak soup - This soup was made of tomato puree filled in with chopped veggies like mushroom, carrot etc was little greasy but good in terms of taste.
▪️Thai Raw Papaya Salad - This is a must try salad made with grated raw papaya mixed with bell peppers and grounded peanuts tossed with chef special sauce was tasty and healthy.

Appetizers
▪️Cottage cheese with ginger chilly sauce dry was an amazing soft paneer starter tossed in ginger chilly sauce and garnished with seasame seeds was yumm and totally awesome. (must try)
▪️Spring Roll - A well prepared fried rolls stuffed with grated carrot and cabbage was good in terms of taste.
▪️Baby Corn Salt & Papper - Deep fried babycorns cooked with spring onions, celery, ginger, garlic and plenty of black peppercorns was moreish and flavoursome.

Mains
▪️Yang Chow FriedRice - A fried rice with chopped veggies and cut roasted cashews were palatable.
▪️Water chestnuts with Green Pepper in sweet bean chilly sauce was delicious gravy preparation that added more taste with fried rice.

Mocktails
▪️Blue Heaven - A fizzy Mocktail made of blue curacao, lime and soda served in tall glass was iced and refreshing.
▪️Strawberry Sorbet - A perfectly made Margarita with crushed ice in strawberry flavour was chilled, sweet and awesome in taste.

Dessert 🍮
▪️Batter Fried Apple with honey served with vanilla icecream was something different and yummy. A great dessert to end the delish meal

The hospitality was superb right from warm greeting when I entered the place followed by royal treatment in terms of service by well mannered staff.
An Excellent and Elite place to enjoy drinks and food.

featured_reviews.review_text:
The phrase  “ Old is Gold “ truly applies to Ambassador Hotel located in Churchgate

Visited Society Restaurant inside Ambassador Hotel after ages to try their new oriental cuisine & the moment you step in you’ll be blown away with the elegance & class this place possesses.

My Veg Order was as follows : -

STARTERS

* Cottage Cheese in ginger chilli garlic sauce - Soft , Chunky pieces of paneer tossed in medium spicy chilli paste with the addition of ginger .
* Spring roll - 6 decent pieces of traditional spring rolls served with salad dressing, chilli & Schezwan sauce.

MAINS

* Gang kiew warn - Similar to Thai green curry which was served with steam rice. Mild in taste & flavours were well balanced. Blended beautifully with steam rice 🍚

* Assorted vegetables with Schezwan
Fresh assorted veggies such as broccoli, spinash, asparagus, pok choy & baby corn tossed in Schezwan gravy . Spicy & tasty 😋

DESSERT

* Chilled lychee with ice cream - Fresh & chilled lychee layered between their in house ice cream.

MOCKTAIL

* Appletini - Non alcoholic version of Apple martini which contains ice, apple syrup & club soda with a couple of apple slices put on top.

The decor oozes with elegance, beautiful wall paintings, traditional Chandeliers & soothing music playing in the background.

In terms of food quality, quantity & service the resturant is flawless & provides a memorable food experience.

Had a memorable dinner experience.

featured_reviews.name: Pankaj Kaklotar
featured_reviews.review_text:
A place that will take you back to the vintage Mumbai (Bombay)

The Society one of the restaurants and part of  ambassador hotel, is very classy and has very soothing ambience. We went to this place for a Saturday Lunch and we spent almost 3 to 4 hours talking, enjoying food and drinks.! Definitely one of the best place which will make you indulge in your conversations with friends, family and you won't realize the time.!

Talking more about Ambience, the society is a fine dine restaurant which makes you super comfortable in terms of seating! Beautiful bar counter, some green plants in corners and overall calmness flows through the place.!

Staff and Service! Mr. Om just made our day by that warm welcome with a big smile on his face. Staff at this place was very polite and well trained. Service was satisfying.!

Food and Drinks! Place offers a wide range of continental and oriental cuisines.! We just tried their oriental menu and it was satisfying overall. We could try few dishes, everything was prepared with fresh and high quality ingredients.!

Som tam - a very popular raw papaya salad with some cherry tomatoes and lot of spices.! Yeah, this is medium spicy salad with lot of health benifits.! If you haven't tried this one yet, go for it.!

Clear wonton soup - soup was good overall only thing I found wrong according to me was excessive layers of wonton in the soup.! If that could be little lesser would make it perfect. Taste wise it was perfect.!

Cottage cheese & Mushroom in Ginger chilly sauce - fresh cottage cheese and juicy mushrooms tossed perfectly in hot and spicy ginger chilly sauce, served piping hot, this was absolutely delightful.
*** Highly Recommended ***

Dimsums (shu mai style) - open head dimsums make it easy to stuff with sauces of choice and were perfectly steamed with fresh veggies stuffing.! Taste wise it was upto the mark.!

Eggplant cakes in hot bean sauce - so many dishes are there which would change your perception about eggplant.! This is one of them.! Those deep fried cakes were perfectly crisp and hot bean sauce was just enhancing taste like anything.! Overall a delicious dish.!

Waterchestnut in a sweet bean sauce - who all are fans of waterchestnuts? Don't miss this super delicious mains with juicy waterchestnuts and sweet bean sauce. Goes very well with the fried rice.!

Veg. Fried Rice - to accompany waterchestnuts and eggplant cake we ordered a veg friend rice. It was perfect fried rice I would say! Vegetables and rice everything in appropriate proportion.!

Whatever the scenario may be! There is always space for some desserts.! The Society has few unique and delightful desserts.!

Fried pan cakes - pan cakes stuffed with dates and deep fried! Served along with chocolate decor.! Tastes amazing and that crispness makes it more enjoyable.! Loved the presentation.!

Overall, a very calm place with some delicious otiental and continental delicacies. A good place for casual and official meet ups.!

We waited for more than 45 minutes after placing our order, yet no food was served. Despite multiple follow-ups with the staff and management, there was little concern shown and no proper update on the delay. Customers should not have to repeatedly chase the staff just to get basic service.

To make matters worse, some of the plates and serving ware appeared chipped and damaged, which raises serious concerns about hygiene and attention to detail.

While the food itself was good when it finally arrived, the poor service, lack of communication, and overall management of the dining experience completely overshadowed it. A restaurant's responsibility goes beyond good food it also includes timely service, cleanliness, and customer care, all of which were lacking during this visit.

featured_reviews.name: Dr. Aman Bhonsle
featured_reviews.review_text:
I’ve been coming here since I was a kid—long enough that I’m pretty sure my first real chicken tandoori happened right here. The menu has changed over the years, sure, but the place has stubbornly refused to lose its old-school charm. Portions? Still generous. This isn’t food that apologizes for itself.

The Chinese starters have absolutely nothing to do with China—and thank God for that. They’re loud, greasy, Indo-Chinese comfort bombs that slap hard. Pick any of the chicken gravies and you’re in a good place emotionally. I will say this: the kebabs feel a little smaller than they used to. Shrinkflation? Age? Betrayal? I don’t know. Still good. Just… noted.

Twenty-one years ago, when I was a broke college student and my parents would leave town—trusting me alone at home far more than they should have—I ordered from here like it was a civic duty. My friends from that era still remember how much food I could put away from this place. This is not health food. No one here is pretending otherwise. But it hits all the right buttons.

I ordered so often that before food apps, before algorithms, the guy answering the phone knew my order just by hearing my voice. Within an hour, like clockwork, the food would land at my parents’ place. I’d sit there demolishing it while binge-watching American TV, living my best irresponsible life.

Some of my old favorites are gone now, but the current menu holds its own. I’ve eaten here with my wife, with her family, across decades and phases of life. Parking is usually manageable. There’s a mosque nearby, Bombay Hospital around the corner, and the now-shuttered Liberty Cinema—where I watched half my childhood movies. The area isn’t glamorous. It doesn’t try to be. It’s old Mumbai, still breathing, still feeding people properly.

This place survives because it’s trusted. Because it’s consistent. Because people who know food still show up here quietly and eat without drama.

What’s instantly noticeable is who eats here.
Old-school locals, serious food people, and a steady stream of expats—especially Arab expats—who clearly didn’t wander in by accident.

Late at night, you’ll see many happy Muslim families settling in comfortably, sharing plates, unhurried, treating the place like an extension of home.

Go without hesitation.
Ask the manager what to order.

Then sit down and let them take care of you.

I recently visited Relish International Veg Cuisine and had a wonderful dining experience. The restaurant offers a great variety of pure vegetarian dishes inspired by different international flavors, all prepared with fresh ingredients and perfect seasoning.

The ambiance is clean, comfortable, and family-friendly, making it a great place for both casual meals and special gatherings. The staff is polite, attentive, and ensures quick service without compromising quality.

What truly stands out is the taste—every dish feels thoughtfully prepared, with balanced flavors and good presentation. The portion sizes are satisfying, and the pricing is reasonable for the quality offered.

Overall, Relish International Veg Cuisine is a fantastic spot for vegetarian food lovers who want something a little different and flavorful. I would definitely recommend it and look forward to visiting again.

featured_reviews.name: Nomnomnoted
featured_reviews.review_text:
Flavor-Filled Family Spot: A Must-Try for All

This restaurant’s menu is packed with flavor—whether you’re diving into their sandwiches or sipping on their floats, you’re in for a treat. Impressively, their Jain options are just as commendable, making this place a hit for everyone. Portion sizes are generous, so be warned: the jacket potatoes (served with gravy!) and the sizzler are huge. Unless you’re absolutely starving, you might want to go easy on the ordering.
Recommended dishes : Sichuan Marbles, Hummus Platter (even jain was excellent)
The shooters here are basically fun-flavored sodas, guaranteed to entertain the kids. Every dish packs adequate flavor and seasoning, and I’d give them all a solid 4/5. The only letdown was the mac and cheese, but everything else was fantastic. After my meal, I needed a walk—that’s how filling it all was! The ambience is that of a classic family restaurant, and even during busy hours, service was prompt. Can’t wait to return on my next vacation.

Ratings
Food: ⭐⭐⭐⭐☆
Drinks: ⭐⭐⭐⭐☆
Ambience: ⭐⭐⭐⭐☆
Value for Money: ⭐⭐⭐⭐☆

TL;DR: Flavorful eats, huge portions, fun drinks, and solid service. A 4/5 across the board—just skip the mac and cheese.

featured_reviews.review_text: The food here is genuinely delicious, and the portion sizes are very satisfying. While weekends can get a bit crowded, it’s absolutely worth the wait. Great quality & great value.

featured_reviews.name: nikesh madhani
featured_reviews.review_text: Relish is truly a gem for pure vegetarian food lovers in Churchgate. With its legacy as one of Mumbai’s oldest multicuisine veg restaurants, Relish consistently delivers both on taste and variety. Located just steps from the newly constructed Churchgate metro station, it’s incredibly easy to find—making it a go-to spot.The menu is a vegetarian’s dream, spanning everything from sizzlers and burgers to pasta, cheesy fondue, and world cuisines like Italian, Mexican, and Continental. Whether you eat Jain or simply want a hearty veg meal, you’re spoiled for choice here. We visited on a bustling Sunday afternoon and, to our delight, there was no wait for a family table—quite a feat given how popular this place can get. Every dish we ordered in Jain style was delicious, and the staff were prompt, polite, and knowledgeable.A thoughtful touch: they even offer bento cakes, which made our family birthday celebration extra special. Valet parking is available, with BMC parking charges of Rs. 100. The only area for improvement? The menu lacks a few options for toddlers—something the restaurant could enhance. Nevertheless, the lively, well-utilized space and inviting ambiance make it perfect for big get-togethers. If you arrive with cousins or friends, order a wide selection so everyone can sample the best Relish has to offer.Relish is a must-visit for anyone craving memorable, high-quality vegetarian fare in South Mumbai. Highly recommended!

I visited this place with my best friend on a Thursday evening this week.

It turned out to be their Thursday candle light dinner special with guitar and live singing, which we were not aware of.

If you order alcohol. You get unlimited Chakna (sides slong-with the alcohol), i.e., Salted peanuts, green salad, corn salad and papad with green chutney, all of this unlimited. They refill as soon as they see the bowls are empty.

Order took time to arrive, but continuous chakna refills made it easier to wait.

Staff is courteous and polite.

We ordered:
* Panchratna fried chicken 3/5 (they should serve this with a honey mustard dip or a tandoori Mayo dip, but they don't serve this with a dip by default). If you ask for a ketchup or a Schezwan sauce, you ll get it with no extra charges (points for that).

* Panchratna classic chicken Biryani, served  since decades 3/5

Location of the bar is a bit tricky as it is slightly inside the lane. Just get into the lane adjacent to Jaffer Bhai restaurant in Marine Lines, close to Bombay Hospital and you will see the bar right infront of you on the left hand side.

Overall. It was a very nice experience, must visit with friends or family.

Please note, my experience was totally based on a Thursday evening live singing vibe. Other days might have a different vibe.

The aamras here is hands down one of the best in the city—fresh, rich, and perfectly sweet. Paired with hot puris, it’s pure comfort on a plate. The rest of the food is equally good, making it a solid spot for a satisfying meal.

Prices are decent, the service is quick, and everything feels clean and well-maintained.

Simple, satisfying, and consistently good—this place never disappoints.

It's unlimited   with a large number of items, the preparation and taste is good.  The waiters are smartly dressed and present a good service.  Visited this restaurant many times.  Apart from thali have tried their biryani which tastes good.  Nice atmosphere where one can enjoy food.  Weekends and holidays will have wait time.  There is a small waiting area outside.  There are paid parking (roadside) on the CCI ( cricket club of India) and other nearby roads which I suggest to be used as traffic police crane regularly makes rounds in this area. The Cuisine here is Indian and they specialize in Kebabs and North Indian Curries. I have tried a lot of Vegetarian dishes here, which is mentioned in detail below.

Truffled Mushroom Baby Kulcha

Small Soft Kulchas Stuffed with a Mushroom Paste. It comes straight out of the tandoor to your plate! It was very soft when I tried it and it had a very mild flavor from the Mushrooms. However, I couldn't taste truffle anywhere, I was expecting the use of some truffle oil at least.

Chili Cheese Baby Kulcha

Another version of Soft Kulchas Stuffed with Cheese and lots of Red Chili Powder, I could taste a lot of cheese and the spice from the Red Chili was also not overpowering. I would prefer this over the Mushroom kulcha even though I LOVE Mushrooms.

Jaituni Paneer Tikka

Giant Cubes of Paneer Marinated in Tandoori Marinate and it was sliced from between to stuff in some Olives. That gave it a tangy flavor and it was an amazing way of serving the Paneer Tikka. The only thing I didn't like is the quantity of Olives was very less and I could hardly taste any Olives.

Kumbh Dak Banglow

Button Mushrooms marinated in a Mustard Paste and cooked inside the tandoor until they become soft.

Daal Makhani

A bowl full of richness, it was exactly what you expect from a Daal Makhani. Melt in mouth Daal in tonne loads of Butter & Cream with superb flavors coming from spices like Clove, Cumin and Cardamom.

Lehsooni Palak

A very creamy concoction of Spinach and Fried Garlic, this was hands down the best dish which I had here. It is a must try if you love Spinach.

The service here was very quick and the staff had total knowledge about the Menu. Overall this place was amazing and I would definitely recommend it to someone who loves to have North Indian Food.

featured_reviews.name: Jatin Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
InterContinental - the iconic Hotel located at Marine Drive is home to Kebab Korner. Kebab Korner is an ultra luxurious fine dine place with breathtaking bayview and serves authentic Indian cuisine along with some fusion dishes / desserts as well. Kebab Korner is located on Level 1 alongside Long & Short, which is a lounge which serves European cuisine.

Kebab Korner has recently introduced Thalis - which is a lavish 3 course Indian meal including appetizers, main course and desserts. They offer Express Lunch Thali which caters to corporate as well and is priced at INR 1800 excluding wine. For dinner they offer "Experience Thali" which is an easy going complete meal, where you can take your time and enjoy scrumptious meal. This is priced at INR 2400.

Heading straight to what was on offer for Experience Thali - Veg

To begin with we were presented with a palate cleanser - Amuse Bouche. Crispy and Spiced Masala Chana Dal packed in edible plastic. I was intrigued about the ingredients used and technique to make this, but it stays as a secret with the restaurant and chef. Very unique and impressed I must say!

We started with Appetizers and were served three of them - Jaipuri Paneer Tikka, Bhune Subz Ki Shami and Sarson Brocolli Tandoori. Paneer Tikka was smoked cottage cheese marinated with olives. The olives gave it a bitter taste for me and I personally love the smokey effect given to cottage cheese. However in this process the cottage cheese might have become a little hard. Something, which can be looked into.

Next we had the Bhune Subz Ki Shami - Round shaped Patties / Tikkis with peas and spiced beans as filling, fried to perfection. Highly recommended to try! After this, we tried the Sarson Broccoli Tandoori - marinated with mustard and grilled to perfection! Loved it! Must try!

Before heading into the mains, we were served another palate cleanser - this time around it was Mango & Lemon Sorbet served in a cutting chai glass. Loved the combination and was very refreshing. Again very unique!

And now coming to the Star Veg Thali at Kebeb Korner - 5 Vegetables and 1 Dal with Assorted Indian Breads along with choice of steamed rice / Khichdi. The thali was presented in a beautiful way. They have a shiny steel arc where all the individual bowls are placed. So all of these 6 bowls along with a bowl of salad is placed in front of you at one go, unlike other thali places where different people serve you continuously which can be irritating at times.

The best part here at Kebab Korner is that you get a thali experience without any hassles. Coming to the 5 vegetables - Bhuna Gobi Masala, Paneer Butter Masala, Subz Miloni, Lehsooni Palak and Beawar Bhindi. Amongst the five my preference would be Beawar Bhindi, Bhuna Gobi Masala and Paneer Butter Masala. Crisp Bhindi (lady fingers) with perfect potli masalas and cherry tomato. Personally I am not a fan of Bhindi, but with the way it was made and tasted, loved it.

Bhuna Gobi Masala, chopped cauliflower tossed with Indian spices and Paneer Butter Masala -creamy cottage cheese in a rich onion and tomato gravy, both came a close second for me.

Dal in the thali was Kebab Korner Signature Dal Makhani. Creamy Black Lentils Dal to be enjoyed with Indian Assorted breads as well as with Steam rice. Tasted real nice. I also tried the Khichdi, could be a good light option after heavy meal.

Finally moving to the desserts, we had the Gulab Jamun and Gulkand Pannacotta - a fantastic fusion of Indian and Italian desserts! Sweet thickened cream topped with Gulkand and Gulkand! Loved the dessert, must try and highly recommended! And towards the end we were presented with a platter of paan - Meetha (Sweet) and Saada (Plain). Couldnt have asked for more!

Overall, if I need to define my experience at Kebab Korner in one word, it will be awestruck! Beautiful setting, lip smacking food, fantastic service, soothing music, one of the most memorable experiences I have had!

featured_reviews.name: Anand Mishra (DocAndy)
featured_reviews.review_text:
Stadium Restaurant has always carried a legacy as a classic Parsi eatery in South Mumbai, and expectations are naturally high when you walk in. Unfortunately, the recent experience was quite disappointing and far from what the name represents.
To begin with, a major portion of the menu was unavailable due to a gas issue. No Chinese items and most veg dishes were not being served. While operational issues can happen, there was no proactive communication or effort from the staff to guide customers properly.
We ordered the basics – Bun Maska, Brun Maska, Special Tea, and a Cheese Sandwich.
Bun Maska & Special Tea: This was the only saving grace. The tea had a nice flavor and the bun was fresh. However, the quantity of maska (butter) has reduced significantly compared to what Stadium was known for.
Brun Maska: Very average. The brun itself was fine, but the maska was almost missing – defeating the whole purpose of ordering it.
Cheese Sandwich: Extremely disappointing. It was literally just a slice of cheese placed between bread with poor presentation. No effort, no taste, no value – completely unacceptable.
Service & Ambience:
The service felt lifeless and unresponsive. There was no warmth, no attentiveness, and overall the environment felt dull and uninviting. For a place with such a legacy, this was shocking.
Overall Impression:
It feels like the restaurant is running purely on its old reputation rather than current quality. If things continue like this, it will only dilute the strong legacy they once built.
A Parsi restaurant like Stadium should reflect discipline, consistency, and warmth, but unfortunately, none of that was evident during this visit.
Final Verdict:
⚠️ Needs serious improvement in food quality, service, and management.
If they wish to survive further, these gaps need immediate attention.

featured_reviews.review_text: Visited this restaurant located in churchgate as it was close to stadium. It was already crowded and had waiting time of around 10mins. featured_reviews.name: Arin Paul
featured_reviews.review_text:
Cafe Bharat, Churchgate, is one of those old-school vegetarian cafés that quietly survives on routine rather than hype. No frills, no experiments, just straightforward food and a steady crowd of office-goers and regulars.

We had Puri Bhaji, Coffee, and Tikki Chole. The puri bhaji was simple and filling, nothing exceptional but nothing to complain about either. The bhaji was mildly spiced, homely in taste, and the puris were fresh enough. The tikki chole was decent; the tikkis were soft and the chole had a familiar North Indian flavour, though it didn’t stand out in any special way. The coffee was basic café-style, served hot, doing its job without trying to impress.

What works in Cafe Bharat’s favour is its budget-friendly pricing, quick service, and convenient location near Churchgate. It’s not a place you’d go out of your way to visit, but if you’re in the area and want a quick, affordable vegetarian meal, it does the job.

The ambience is functional and old-fashioned; clean, but clearly built for efficiency rather than comfort or aesthetics. Service is prompt and no-nonsense.

Overall, Cafe Bharat is reliable, modest, and predictable. Nothing great, nothing bad. Just a simple veg café that knows its role and sticks to it. Suitable for a quick bite, not for culinary excitement.

featured_reviews.name: Sachin Talwalkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
A 70-year-old iconic establishment of South Bombay, it has long been at the center of fine dining for stars and socialites alike. It was frequently patronized by the likes of Raj Kapoor, Dilip Kumar, and many cricketers. Recently renovated, you step into a regal experience - complete with uniformed waitstaff, European Art Deco accents, and live music.

The menu offers a unique mix of Indian dishes, a few European selections, and non-alcoholic beverages. Unique, because an ambience like this almost demands a glass of wine - something you sorely miss as piano renditions of old and new Bollywood compositions play on.

The food is excellent, the service could be better, but the experience is a must-have. One that transports you back to the charm of old Bombay.

featured_reviews.name: Anannya
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re looking for a place that blends old-school charm with a premium, aesthetic vibe, this is the one. I visited this iconic spot near Marine Lines and honestly, the ambience itself sets the mood. Loved the seating and the service.

What we tried:
Summer Breeze 4.5⭐
Quattro Formaggi  5⭐

The pasta was the highlight as it was runny, rich and sauce. The portion size would be easily filling for two. The mocktail could’ve been sweeter, but still enjoyable.

Make a reservation if you’re planning to go on weekends or during peak dinner hours, it gets busy. Overall, I would rate a 5/5. Definitely going back to explore more on the menu.

featured_reviews.name: Mahesh Maurya
featured_reviews.review_text:

On the positive side, the environment and ambiance of the restaurant were quite good—clean, comfortable, and pleasant for dining with friends or family. The staff was polite, and considering the location, the prices are affordable and value for money.

If the restaurant could focus on improving the quality of service, especially ensuring that the food is served hot, it would definitely enhance the overall dining experience.

The menu is diverse and delicious, and includes a wide range of delicious Indian dishes.  The food was excellently prepared and used fresh ingredients and authentic flavours.  I enjoyed trying different dishes like biryani, tikka and curry.

featured_reviews.name: Sandeep Samtani
featured_reviews.review_text: We set out on a magnificent culinary adventure at the newly launched Pali Bhavan at Eros, a true gastronomic treasure that shines bright with its sublime Indian cuisine. The ambiance was very laid back, bathed in a warm glow by colonial decor and softly radiant lights. Our delightful odyssey commenced with Tandoori pomfret, Galouti kebab, Malai chicken tikka, and prawn, each dish a brilliant testament to the chef's innovative genius. The main course showcased their legendary crab Sukkha and Kali Dal, masterfully crafted to exhilarate the senses. The crowning glory was the paan kulfi and chocolate roshogolla, desserts that left us utterly enchanted. The food was truly sublime, with flavors that joyfully danced on the palate and desserts that stole the spotlight, rendering the entire experience profoundly unforgettable.

featured_reviews.name: Lewis Crombie
featured_reviews.review_text:
Simply the best Indian food I've ever eaten. I've visited twice and everything I've ordered and been recommended has been delicious.

Service was quick and smooth and the setting is gorgeous. The restaurant looks completely innocuous from the outside but inside is very well decorated and welcoming.

The Gunpowerd Potatoes were perfectly spiced. A real standout dish and I'll be ordering a portion every time I visit.

featured_reviews.name: Dan Liu
featured_reviews.review_text: Adding this place to the must eat list on our next trip back.  All the dishes were fantastic and the the ice cream with a floral taste was one of the most unique dishes I’ve tried, loved it!  The set up is pretty cool and I can’t wait to go back

featured_reviews.name: Aakash
featured_reviews.review_text:
There’s an unmistakable old-world charm here; an almost nostalgic, lived-in elegance that feels refreshingly authentic in a city that often chases the new and shiny.

The ambience is wonderfully understated: warm lighting, vintage touches, wooden furniture that has seen stories, and that classic Bombay colonial-meets-Bandra vibe.

The food is rich, deeply flavoured, cooked with real care. Every dish carries that unmistakable depth; nothing is timid or overly polished. The spicing is confident, the portions generous, and the execution consistent. It’s the kind of meal that lingers in memory long after you’ve left.

Whether it’s a quiet celebration, a catch-up with old friends, or simply craving something soulful, Pali Bhavan delivers exactly what one hopes for in a neighbourhood favourite: character, flavour, and comfort in equal measure.

Highly recommended for those who appreciate substance over spectacle.

featured_reviews.name: Paul
featured_reviews.review_text: This is a lovely restaurant with absolutely amazing food. Every dish we had was fantastic - some of the best food we have had whilst in India. Friendly and attentive staff and the restaurant has a lovely atmosphere. Highly recommended for anyone visiting Mumbai

featured_reviews.name: JM Prevost
featured_reviews.review_text:
Feel like I was unknowingly looking for this curry my whole life.

Nepalese Dumplings were the most surprising and excellent. Served with a carrot chutney with a hidden bit of spicy kick.

Traditional chicken curry was good enough to drink.

So pleased.

featured_reviews.name: Monis
featured_reviews.review_text:
Stepping into Pali Bhavan is less like walking into a restaurant and more like being welcomed into a world carefully curated for the senses. The moment you cross the threshold, a warm, vibrant energy wraps around you — the kind that hums with quiet excitement and makes you instantly glad you came. The interiors are a masterclass in rustic vintage design: weathered textures, artful nostalgia, and thoughtful details that together create an atmosphere that feels both timeless and distinctly alive.

The food is, simply put, exceptional. Every dish arrives as evidence of a kitchen that takes its craft seriously — where quality is not a checkbox but a standard. The menu reads like a love letter to bold, imaginative cooking: innovative, eye-catching, and refreshingly unhurried in its approach. Dish after dish finds a way to surprise, with flavours that linger long after the last bite and an unmistakable ability to awaken the palate in ways you didn't expect.

Equally deserving of praise is the service. The staff carries a warmth that feels genuine — attentive without being intrusive, welcoming without being performative. They move through the room with ease, and their care for the guest experience is palpable. Dining here never once feels rushed; instead, it unfolds at exactly the right pace for a truly relaxed, enjoyable evening.

"Pali Bhavan doesn't just offer a meal — it offers an experience worthy of returning to. South Mumbai has quietly welcomed a new icon, and those who discover it will find themselves planning their next visit before the first one is even over."

The drinks were amazing as well, and the staff were all incredibly sweet and welcoming throughout the evening. The only issue we had was with one dish we ordered that never arrived. We asked about it twice and were told they would check on it, but it still didn’t come, so we ended up ordering another plate of sushi while we waited.

Thankfully, the missing dish wasn’t added to our bill, so no complaints there. It was a small hiccup, and I’d just suggest being a bit more mindful with orders, but apart from that everything was lovely.

The food we did receive was great, the atmosphere was stunning, and overall it was a really enjoyable dining experience.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited this place with my friends after hearing a lot about it, and it truly lived up to the expectations. We had a fantastic experience—both the food and the overall vibe were excellent.

We ordered Bombil fry as a starter, along with Prawns Thali and Surmai Thali. Every single dish was 10/10. Personally, whenever I try a new place for fish, I judge it by the taste of the Bombil fry—and this one was outstanding. It was extremely fresh, perfectly crispy, and the masala was well balanced and nicely blended.

The same quality and freshness reflected in the Surmai and Prawns thali—authentic taste and very satisfying portions.

On the owner’s suggestion, we also tried their Mutton Thali for a change, and it was surprisingly excellent. The mutton was fresh, tender, and full of flavour, which is rare to find these days.

If you’re a seafood lover, this place is a must-visit. Highly recommended for anyone looking to enjoy quality fish with great taste and vibes.
